[RDSC.5.8.3] `proto_source` is the .proto text generated by
the compiler from the schema declaration. The compiler **must** declare
the field of every nullable slot (`T?`, the `Slot` atom's `nullable`
flag, [LNUL.3.1]) as a proto3 `optional` field, so that its presence is
explicit, and **must not** declare any other field `optional`. It **must**
declare each slot's field with the proto3 type [RDSC.5.8.7] gives the slot's
kind. A fact-reference slot's is `uint64` because a recorded fact body carries
the referenced fact's handle there ([RFCS.6.3]), and the temporal kinds' is
`int64` because they are Int-represented ([RDSC.5.5.8]). The runtime stores
the text verbatim (the body is `COMPRESSION_NONE`, [RDSC.4.4]); consumers (storage adapters, replayers,
debug tools) read it from the loaded engine via the
integrator-facing surface.

**The text names the message for the schema's own name** ([LIMP.13.1]). The
message is the schema's `NAME`, and the package is `ds.dsc.user.v1`, followed for
a library's schema by the library's path: `plant.sensors.Reading` is the message
`Reading` in `package ds.dsc.user.v1.plant.sensors`. So two libraries' schemas
of one `NAME` are two messages in one descriptor pool.

**A synthetic schema's `proto_source` is empty.** Its
name ([LLEX.10.6.1]) can't be a protobuf message name, and its facts never cross
a boundary: none reaches a stream ([RFCS.5.1]), so nothing needs their wire
shape.
